# Model Summary

LoRA adapter for Brazilian Portuguese institutional brand-voice compliance, fine-tuned on **Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct** (70B parameters) via [Adaption's](https://adaptionlabs.ai) AutoScientist platform. Given a raw/informal citizen request and an explicit Brand Voice Guide, the model rewrites the response as a fully compliant formal institutional communication — correct structure, impersonal institutional voice, required vocabulary, and no banned informal markers.

Submitted to the **AutoScientist Challenge 2026** (Marketing category).

## Usage

This is a LoRA adapter. Load it on top of the base model using the PEFT library:

```python
from peft import PeftModel
from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer

base_model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained("meta-llama/Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct")
tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained("meta-llama/Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct")

model = PeftModel.from_pretrained(
    base_model,
    "/kaggle/input/vozbr-brandvoice-adapter/other/lora-adapter-for-pt-br-institutional-brand-voice-compliance/1"
)

prompt = """GUIA DE VOZ DE MARCA - COMUNICACAO INSTITUCIONAL FORMAL (PT-BR)
[... guide omitted for brevity ...]

Um cidadao enviou a seguinte solicitacao. Reescreva como comunicacao
oficial do orgao responsavel, seguindo o guia de voz de marca:

Um cidadao relata que sua aposentadoria nao foi paga no mes de marco
e pede explicacao urgente."""

inputs = tokenizer(prompt, return_tensors="pt")
outputs = model.generate(**inputs, max_new_tokens=512)
print(tokenizer.decode(outputs[0], skip_special_tokens=True))
```

**Input:** A Brand Voice Guide (structure, tone, required vocabulary, banned terms) plus a raw/informal citizen request, in Brazilian Portuguese.
**Output:** A formal institutional response in pt-BR following the guide — formal opener, objective context, explanatory body with protocol/deadline references, closing with a follow-up channel, and institutional identification.

**Known limitations:** Fine-tuned on data derived from federal-ombudsman (CGU/Fala.BR) correspondence. The Brand Voice Guide and conformance rubric are designed to generalize to corporate/institutional communication, but the underlying register reflects formal government correspondence. Personal data in training examples is templated/placeholder (e.g. `[Nome do Requerente]`, `[CPF]`), not real citizen data.

## System

Standalone LoRA adapter. Requires the base model `meta-llama/Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct` to be loaded first via PEFT.

## Implementation requirements

- **Training platform:** Adaption AutoScientist (cloud compute)
- **Base model size:** 70B parameters (Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct)
- **Training method:** SFT + LoRA (all-linear modules)
- **Training config:** 113 steps · 1 epoch · cosine schedule · lr 1e-4 · warmup ratio 0.03 · max grad norm 1
- **Inference:** Requires GPU with sufficient VRAM for Llama-3.3-70B (4-bit quantization recommended for single-GPU inference)

---

# Model Characteristics

## Model initialization

Fine-tuned from `meta-llama/Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct` using LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation). Base model weights are frozen; only the LoRA adapter weights are trained.

## Model stats

| Parameter | Value |
|---|---|
| Base model | Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct |
| Base model size | 70B parameters |
| LoRA rank (r) | 64 |
| LoRA alpha | 128 |
| LoRA dropout | 0 |
| Trainable modules | all-linear |
| Optimizer / schedule | cosine, lr 1e-4, warmup ratio 0.03 |

## Other details

No pruning or quantization applied to the adapter weights. Adapter trained in full precision via Adaption AutoScientist infrastructure.

---

# Data Overview

## Training data

**Dataset:** [Fernandosr85/vozbr-brandvoice](https://huggingface.co/datasets/Fernandosr85/vozbr-brandvoice) (base, 6,505 pairs) · expanded to 20,204 rows via Adaption Adaptive Data augmentation (8,000 domain-specific + 5,700 general-purpose data points) — published as [Fernandosr85/adaption-pt-br-formal-gov-complaints](https://huggingface.co/datasets/Fernandosr85/adaption-pt-br-formal-gov-complaints), the dataset actually used for training.

The base dataset is derived from [FalaBR-SynthLetters](https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/fernandosr85/falabr-synthletters-enhanced-br-ombudsman) (CGU/Fala.BR federal ombudsman correspondence, formal pt-BR letters). Each example pairs:

- **Prompt:** An explicit Brand Voice Guide (10-point structure/tone/vocabulary rules) plus a reframed raw citizen request.
- **Completion:** A formal institutional response, pre-filtered to score ≥ 7/10 on a deterministic 10-point Brand Voice conformance rubric (`formal_opener`, `institutional_voice`, `process_vocab`, `progress_vocab`, `followup_vocab`, `formal_closing`, `no_banned_terms`, `no_excess_caps`, `min_length`, `no_first_person_singular`).

Dataset remastered by Adaption Adaptive Data pipeline: **Grade A (9.4/10) · +17.5% quality improvement**, governance domain percentile 16.7 → 57.7.

## Demographic groups

Dataset derived from structured/synthetic Brazilian federal-ombudsman correspondence. No individual citizen demographic data is used; all personal identifiers in training examples are templated placeholders (e.g. `[Nome do Requerente]`, `[CPF]`).

## Evaluation data

No explicit train/test split. Evaluation performed by Adaption AutoScientist's training winrate metric on held-out internal comparisons.

---

# Evaluation Results

## Summary

| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| Base model wins | 21 |
| Adapted model wins | 79 |
| Adapted model win rate | **79%** |
| Adaptive Data quality score | 8.0 → 9.4 (+17.5%) |
| Dataset quality grade | B → **A** |
| Percentile (Governance domain) | 16.7 → 57.7 |
| Training | LoRA r=64/alpha=128 · 113 steps · 1 epoch · cosine schedule |

**Note on win rate:** Unlike a knowledge-dense reasoning task, brand-voice compliance is primarily structural/stylistic — formal opener, impersonal institutional voice, required vocabulary, banned-term avoidance, formal closing. This is exactly the kind of pattern LoRA fine-tuning transfers well, and the 79% vs 21% win rate reflects the adapted model consistently producing responses that match the explicit Brand Voice Guide, where the base model does not reliably follow it unprompted.

## Subgroup evaluation results

No per-category subgroup breakdown was computed for this submission; the training winrate (79% vs 21%) is reported at the aggregate level by Adaption AutoScientist.

## Fairness

This adapter operationalizes a written Brand Voice Guide into a checkable, deterministic rubric (10 binary checks), so conformance can be audited independently of the model — the same rubric used to filter training data can be used to evaluate any model's outputs.

## Usage limitations

- Fine-tuned on data derived from Brazilian federal-ombudsman correspondence (2021–2024), as of June 2026.
- The Brand Voice Guide reflects a formal government-correspondence register; applying it to other corporate brand voices may require adjusting the guide's required vocabulary and tone rules.
- Not a substitute for legal or compliance review of institutional communications.

## Ethics

Derived from public-sector open data (CGU/Fala.BR, dados.gov.br, CC BY 4.0 → CC BY-SA 4.0). No real citizen personal data is used in training; all personal identifiers are templated placeholders.

---

## Credits

- **Fine-tuning platform:** [Adaption](https://adaptionlabs.ai) — AutoScientist & Adaptive Data
- **Challenge:** [AutoScientist Challenge 2026](https://adaptionlabs.ai/blog/autoscientist-challenge) — Marketing category
- **HuggingFace model:** [Fernandosr85/vozbr-brandvoice-adapter](https://huggingface.co/Fernandosr85/vozbr-brandvoice-adapter)
- **HuggingFace dataset (base, 6,505 pairs):** [Fernandosr85/vozbr-brandvoice](https://huggingface.co/datasets/Fernandosr85/vozbr-brandvoice)
- **HuggingFace dataset (expanded, 20,204 pairs, used for training):** [Fernandosr85/adaption-pt-br-formal-gov-complaints](https://huggingface.co/datasets/Fernandosr85/adaption-pt-br-formal-gov-complaints)
- **Kaggle dataset:** [VozBR-BrandVoice Dataset](https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/fernandosr85/vozbr-brandvoice-dataset)
- **Source dataset:** [FalaBR-SynthLetters](https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/fernandosr85/falabr-synthletters-enhanced-br-ombudsman)
- **Author:** Fernando Rodrigues · [Kaggle: fernandosr85](https://www.kaggle.com/fernandosr85)

A fine-tuned DeBERTa-v3-base model for cyberbullying and toxic text 
detection, trained on 75,000 balanced social media and news portal texts 
across 4 platforms (Facebook, Instagram, Reddit, News Portal).

# ── Model Details ──────────────────────────────────────

Base Model     : microsoft/deberta-v3-base
Task           : Multi-class Text Classification
Classes        : 7
Training Data  : 75,000 texts (perfectly balanced)
Val Accuracy   : 100% (balanced_accuracy_score = 1.0)
Framework      : TensorFlow / Keras
Max Seq Length : 128 tokens

# ── Classes ────────────────────────────────────────────

0 → Harassment_Stalking
1 → Homophobia_LGBTQphobia
2 → Misogyny_Sexism
3 → Non_Toxic
4 → Profanity_Insult
5 → Racism_Xenophobia
6 → Religious_Hate

# ── Training Details ───────────────────────────────────

Optimizer      : AdamW (lr=2e-5, weight_decay=0.01)
Loss           : SparseCategoricalCrossentropy
Epochs         : 4 (early stopping)
Batch Size     : 32
Hardware       : Tesla P100-PCIE-16GB GPU
Training Time  : ~1.5 hours

# ── Architecture ───────────────────────────────────────

DeBERTa-v3-base backbone
→ Mean pooling over last hidden state
→ Dropout (0.1)
→ Dense (256, GELU)
→ Dropout (0.1)
→ Dense (7, Softmax)

instances.usage:
# ── Usage ──────────────────────────────────────────────

from transformers import AutoTokenizer
import tensorflow as tf
import numpy as np

tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained('microsoft/deberta-v3-base')
model     = tf.keras.models.load_model('cyberbullying_detector.keras')
classes   = ['Harassment_Stalking', 'Homophobia_LGBTQphobia',
             'Misogyny_Sexism', 'Non_Toxic', 'Profanity_Insult',
             'Racism_Xenophobia', 'Religious_Hate']

def predict(text):
    tokens = tokenizer(text, max_length=128, padding='max_length',
                       truncation=True, return_tensors='tf')
    inputs = {
        'input_ids'      : tokens['input_ids'],
        'attention_mask' : tokens['attention_mask'],
        'token_type_ids' : tf.zeros_like(tokens['input_ids']),
    }
    probs  = model.predict(inputs, verbose=0)
    return classes[np.argmax(probs)]

print(predict("Go back to your country"))
→ Racism_Xenophobia

models.description:
# Model Summary

Crop Care is a **cascade plant-disease classifier** that diagnoses diseases in
five staple crops grown in Ghana: **cashew, cassava, maize, tomato, and cocoa**.
It is built for offline, on-device use by smallholder farmers.

Rather than one multi-output network, Crop Care is a **cascade of independent
EfficientNetB0 models**: a **router** first identifies the crop (the 5 crops plus
an "Other" class), then a per-crop **specialist** classifies the disease. A
Mahalanobis-distance out-of-distribution check and router-confidence thresholds
reject unfamiliar or unsupported inputs instead of forcing a wrong label. Maize
and Cocoa each use a 2-model ensemble (probabilities averaged). Every model is
temperature-calibrated so confidence values are meaningful.

The models were fine-tuned from an ImageNet-pretrained EfficientNetB0 backbone on
the **[crop-care-dataset] (https://kaggle.com/datasets/c18b9b28cc992ed61f2299edc3988c7aa57fd609610953cfef384b0a7379d551)** image dataset. On a held-out test set every crop
clears 90% accuracy (Router 99.4%, Cashew 97.2%, Tomato 97.3%, Cassava 93.8%,
Maize 92.9%, Cocoa 90.2%).

## Usage

Two variations are published: **LiteRT / float16** (TensorFlow Lite, deployment)
and **Keras / cascade** (native `.keras`, for fine-tuning).

**Deployment (LiteRT) — input `[1,H,W,3]` float32 RGB in [0,1]; output raw softmax:**

```python
import json, numpy as np, tensorflow as tf
from PIL import Image

man = json.load(open("calibration.json"))
spec = man["models"]["cashew"]
size = spec["input_size"]                      # 240 (cocoa = 300)

img = Image.open("leaf.jpg").convert("RGB").resize((size, size))
x = (np.asarray(img, np.float32) / 255.0)[None, ...]   # [1, size, size, 3]

it = tf.lite.Interpreter("cashew_float16.tflite"); it.allocate_tensors()
i, o = it.get_input_details()[0], it.get_output_details()[0]
it.set_tensor(i["index"], x); it.invoke()
probs = it.get_tensor(o["index"])[0]           # shape [num_classes], sums to 1
print(spec["class_names"][int(np.argmax(probs))])
```

**Fine-tuning (Keras) — requires the** [`crop-care-project`] (https://kaggle.com/datasets/c18b9b28cc992ed61f2299edc3988c7aa57fd609610953cfef384b0a7379d551) **code on the path:**

```python
import tensorflow as tf
from model.classifier import SingleHeadClassifier        # from crop-care-project-v2
model = tf.keras.models.load_model("cocoa_seed42/final_model.keras", compile=False)
# or re-train any crop:  python train_specialist.py --crop cassava --dataset_root

instances.overview:
**Keras (TensorFlow 2) — native .keras weights, for fine-tuning and research.**

This variation contains the full Crop Care cascade as native Keras checkpoints. Use it to fine-tune, re-train, or inspect the models. To simply deploy and run on-device, use the LiteRT / float16 variation instead.

**IMPORTANT** — you need the [**model code**](https://kaggle.com/datasets/c18b9b28cc992ed61f2299edc3988c7aa57fd609610953cfef384b0a7379d551) to load these.

The models are instances of a custom SingleHeadClassifier class, so a .keras file will not load unless that class is on your Python path. Get it from the crop-care-project dataset (the training/inference code) and attach it alongside this model.

**Contents:**

8 model folders. Each contains final_model.keras (canonical weights), best_model.keras, class_mapping.json (class order), and temperature.json (calibration T).

- router/ — crop router (5 crops + "Other"), input 240x240; also holds mahalanobis.npz (the out-of-distribution detector)
- cashew/, cassava/, tomato/ — disease specialists, input 240x240
- maize_seed42/, maize_seed1337/ — maize specialist (2-model ensemble), input 240x240
- cocoa_seed42/, cocoa_seed1337/ — cocoa specialist (2-model ensemble), input 300x300

Each model is an independent EfficientNetB0 (ImageNet transfer learning), so input size is per-model: cocoa 300x300, all others 240x240. Maize and Cocoa are ensembles — average the two members' probabilities, then argmax. router/mahalanobis.npz is the fitted Mahalanobis out-of-distribution detector used at inference.

**For on-device deployment without the code dependency, use the LiteRT / float16 variation.**

`License: MIT. The trained weights are MIT-licensed; the training data has its own CC BY-NC terms (see the [dataset](https://kaggle.com/datasets/c18b9b28cc992ed61f2299edc3988c7aa57fd609610953cfef384b0a7379d551)`

>Citation: Asaah, M. (2026). Crop Care: A Cascade Plant-Disease Classifier for Ghanaian Staple Crops. KNUST. Kaggle.
instances.usage:
**These .keras models use a custom class, so attach the** [`crop-care-project`](https://kaggle.com/datasets/c18b9b28cc992ed61f2299edc3988c7aa57fd609610953cfef384b0a7379d551) **dataset (the model code) to your notebook before loading.**

**Load a model (requires [crop-care-project](https://kaggle.com/datasets/c18b9b28cc992ed61f2299edc3988c7aa57fd609610953cfef384b0a7379d551) on the path):**
    
    import tensorflow as tf 
    from model.classifier import SingleHeadClassifier   # from crop-care-project

    model = tf.keras.models.load_model(
        "cocoa_seed42/final_model.keras", compile=False)
    print(model.input_size)   # 300 for cocoa, 240 for the rest

**Run a prediction (input: RGB image, [0,1] float32, resized to model.input_size; output: softmax probabilities):**

    import json, numpy as np
    from PIL import Image

    size = model.input_size
    img = Image.open("leaf.jpg").convert("RGB").resize((size, size))
    x = (np.asarray(img, np.float32) / 255.0)[None, ...]
    probs = model(x, training=False).numpy()[0]

    classes = json.load(open("cocoa_seed42/class_mapping.json"))["classes"]
    print(classes[int(np.argmax(probs))], round(float(np.max(probs)), 2))

**Fine-tune or re-train (with the [crop-care-project](https://kaggle.com/datasets/c18b9b28cc992ed61f2299edc3988c7aa57fd609610953cfef384b0a7379d551) code and [crop-care-dataset](https://kaggle.com/datasets/24b575bff1639ac707c925c899f58764fd256519eb97850d22bfef5677c142e6) data):**

    # train or fine-tune any crop specialist
    python train_specialist.py --crop cassava --dataset_root "

instances.overview:
**LiteRT (TensorFlow Lite) Float16 — deployment bundle.**

Self-contained and ready to run on-device. This variation contains 8 TFLite models plus a single calibration.json manifest that tells an app how to run the full cascade. Use this variation to deploy; use the Keras variation to fine-tune.

**Contents**:

- router_float16.tflite — crop router (5 crops + "Other"), input 240x240
- cashew_float16.tflite, cassava_float16.tflite, tomato_float16.tflite — disease specialists, input 240x240
- maize_seed42_float16.tflite, maize_seed1337_float16.tflite — maize specialist (2-model ensemble), input 240x240
- cocoa_seed42_float16.tflite, cocoa_seed1337_float16.tflite — cocoa specialist (2-model ensemble), input 300x300
- calibration.json — per-model temperature, class names, input sizes, ensemble membership, and cascade thresholds

All models output raw softmax. Input size is per-model — Cocoa runs at 300x300, every other model at 240x240, so always read input_size from calibration.json rather than assuming one global size. Float16 keeps each model around 10 MB while preserving accuracy.

**How to use it (single model)**:

    import json, numpy as np, tensorflow as tf
    from PIL import Image

    man = json.load(open("calibration.json"))
    spec = man["models"]["cashew"]
    size = spec["input_size"]   # 240 (cocoa = 300)

    img = Image.open("leaf.jpg").convert("RGB").resize((size, size))
    x = (np.asarray(img, np.float32) / 255.0)[None, ...]

    it = tf.lite.Interpreter("cashew_float16.tflite")
    it.allocate_tensors()
    i = it.get_input_details()[0]
    o = it.get_output_details()[0]
    it.set_tensor(i["index"], x)
    it.invoke()
    probs = it.get_tensor(o["index"])[0]
    print(spec["class_names"][int(np.argmax(probs))])

**Running the full cascade**:

    def run_model(name, x):
        m = man["models"][name]
        it = tf.lite.Interpreter(m["tflite_file"])
        it.allocate_tensors()
        i = it.get_input_details()[0]
        o = it.get_output_details()[0]
        it.set_tensor(i["index"], x)
        it.invoke()
        return it.get_tensor(o["index"])[0], m

    def preprocess(path, size):
        im = Image.open(path).convert("RGB").resize((size, size))
        return (np.asarray(im, np.float32) / 255.0)[None, ...]

    # 1) Router at 240 -> which crop?
    rprobs, rmeta = run_model("router", preprocess("leaf.jpg", 240))
    crop = rmeta["class_names"][int(np.argmax(rprobs))]

    # Reject out-of-distribution inputs
    if (float(np.max(rprobs)) < man["router_confidence_threshold"]
            or crop == man["other_class_label"]):
        print("Rejected: not a supported crop / unclear image")
    else:
        key = crop.lower()
        # 2) Specialist. Ensembles (cocoa, maize) -> average members.
        if key in man["ensembles"]:
            members = man["ensembles"][key]
            size = man["models"][members[0]]["input_size"]
            x = preprocess("leaf.jpg", size)
            probs = np.mean([run_model(mm, x)[0] for mm in members], axis=0)
            classes = man["models"][members[0]]["class_names"]
        else:
            size = man["models"][key]["input_size"]
            probs, meta = run_model(key, preprocess("leaf.jpg", size))
            classes = meta["class_names"]
        print(crop, "->", classes[int(np.argmax(probs))],
              round(float(np.max(probs)), 2))

Calibrated confidence (optional): outputs are raw softmax. For calibrated confidence, divide the model's logits by its temperature (from the manifest) and re-softmax. Temperature never changes the predicted class — only the confidence value.

**Notes**:

- Input must be RGB, [0,1] float32, resized to each model's input_size.
- Cocoa runs at 300x300, all others at 240x240 — read it from the manifest.
- For cocoa and maize, run all ensemble members and average before argmax.
- This is a standalone deployment bundle; it does not need the model code to run. (The Keras variation does, for loading the custom model class.)
instances.usage:
Run a single specialist (input: RGB image, [0,1] float32, resized to the model's input_size; output: raw softmax probabilities):

    import json, numpy as np, tensorflow as tf
    from PIL import Image

    man = json.load(open("calibration.json"))
    spec = man["models"]["cashew"]          # any crop, or "router"
    size = spec["input_size"]               # 240 for most, 300 for cocoa

    img = Image.open("leaf.jpg").convert("RGB").resize((size, size))
    x = (np.asarray(img, np.float32) / 255.0)[None, ...]   # [1, size, size, 3]

    it = tf.lite.Interpreter(spec["tflite_file"])
    it.allocate_tensors()
    i = it.get_input_details()[0]
    o = it.get_output_details()[0]
    it.set_tensor(i["index"], x)
    it.invoke()
    probs = it.get_tensor(o["index"])[0]    # sums to 1
    print(spec["class_names"][int(np.argmax(probs))],
          round(float(np.max(probs)), 2))

Full cascade: run the router first (240x240); if its top confidence is below router_confidence_threshold or the class is "Other", reject the image. Otherwise run that crop's specialist at its own input_size. For cocoa and maize (listed in calibration.json["ensembles"]), run all members and average their probabilities before argmax.

Notes:
- Cocoa runs at 300x300; all other models at 240x240. Always read input_size from calibration.json.
- Feed [0,1] float32 RGB. Do not add ImageNet mean/std normalisation — the backbone does its own scaling.
- For calibrated confidence, divide the model's logits by its temperature (from the manifest) and re-softmax; this never changes the predicted class.

models.provenanceSources: Original work by Manasseh Asaah (Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology, Ghana), developed under the supervision of Dr. Kate Takyi. The cascade was fine-tuned from an ImageNet-pretrained EfficientNetB0 backbone (Keras Applications, https://keras.io/api/applications/efficientnet/) using TensorFlow / Keras. Training and inference code is published as the [crop-care-project](https://kaggle.com/datasets/c18b9b28cc992ed61f2299edc3988c7aa57fd609610953cfef384b0a7379d551) dataset; the models were trained on the [crop-care-dataset](https://kaggle.com/datasets/24b575bff1639ac707c925c899f58764fd256519eb97850d22bfef5677c142e6) image dataset. No third-party model weights other than the EfficientNetB0 ImageNet backbone are reused.
